rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: no run finished on any track. Every run ended off_track after very little progress (0.105 oval, 0.15 s-bend, 0.11 slalom). The off-track limit here is effectively 0.06 m, and max_error was about 0.063 m, so the robot drifted just past the edge of the line. Line_loss_events were 1 to 2 per run and steering_oscillation was modest (0.08 to 0.15), while rms_error was low (about 0.026 to 0.029 m). The robot tracks the line well on average but fails at short, sharp excursions, which points to too little damping and a sensor footprint that gives a noisy edge signal. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.3, so the robot can corner and recover from the initial transient without exceeding its tracking margin. (2) kd 0.1 to 0.3, to damp the overshoot that produces the 6 cm excursions. (3) sensor_size 0.008 to 0.012, so the 12 mm sensor pitch overlaps fully and the signal stays nonzero at the tape edge, reducing line-loss events. kp, ki, sensor positions, weights and line_loss stay unchanged to isolate the effect of these three changes. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower max_error, with completion more likely. Cost: a slower base_speed may push completion_time toward or past 3 s, which would be the next thing to tune. Next measurements wanted: max_error and line_loss_events per track, steering_oscillation (to judge whether kd 0.3 is too much), and completion_time (to decide whether base_speed must rise again).
